MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Specimen Type: Bone Marrow Aspirate
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Myeloma with inadequate response to treatment. Sample for clinical trial enrollment.
Clinical Diagnosis: Multiple myeloma

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase FISH Analysis for Multiple Myeloma Panel

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on cultured and uncultured bone marrow cells using the following probe sets:
• GeneProbe LSI D5S23, D5S721/CEP 9/CEP 15
• GeneTrack IGH Plus Breakapart Probe
• GeneTrack CKS1B/CDKN2C(P18)
• OmniPath CLL Kit (DLEU 13q14/13q34, TP53 17p13.1, ATM 11q22.3)

A minimum of 100 interphase nuclei were analyzed for each probe set. Results are reported as the number of abnormal cells per 100 cells examined.

RESULTS

ABNORMAL FINDINGS:

1. MONOSOMY 13
   Probe: DLEU (13q14)/13q34
   Result: Loss of chromosome 13 detected in 87/100 cells (87%)
   Normal Range: <5%

2. CKS1B GAIN
   Probe: CKS1B (1q21)
   Result: Gain of 1-2 additional copies detected in 81/100 cells (81%)
   Normal Range: <5%

3. HYPERDIPLOIDY
   a) CDKN2C (1p32.3): Additional copies in 25/100 cells (25%)
   b) D5S23/D5S721 (5p15.2): Additional copies in 64/100 cells (64%)
   c) CEP9: Additional copies in 74/100 cells (74%)
   d) CEP15: Additional copies in 70/100 cells (70%)

NORMAL FINDINGS:

4. IGH REARRANGEMENT
   Probe: IGH (14q32) Breakapart
   Result: No rearrangement detected
   Normal signal pattern in 100/100 cells examined

5. TP53 DELETION
   Probe: TP53 (17p13.1)
   Result: No deletion detected
   Normal diploid pattern in 100/100 cells examined

6. ATM STATUS
   Probe: ATM (11q22.3)
   Result: Normal diploid pattern
   No deletion detected in 100/100 cells examined

INTERPRETATION
This FISH analysis reveals multiple cytogenetic abnormalities characteristic of multiple myeloma:

• Monosomy 13 (87% of cells): Associated with more aggressive disease course
• Gain of 1q21/CKS1B (81% of cells): Associated with disease progression and adverse prognosis
• Hyperdiploidy with gains of chromosomes 5, 9, and 15: Generally associated with standard risk myeloma when not accompanied by high-risk features
• Absence of IGH rearrangement and TP53 deletion: Favorable prognostic indicators

The combination of monosomy 13 and 1q gain represents an intermediate to high-risk cytogenetic profile in multiple myeloma. These findings provide important disease characterization for clinical trial stratification and treatment planning.

LIMITATIONS
Dual-color break-apart probes will not detect rearrangements from cryptic insertion events, which may occur in a small percentage of cases. This analysis is limited to the genomic regions interrogated by the specific probes used.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
